//: Repo-local Codex CLI hooks for RytmRandomizer — the codex analogue of
.claude/settings.json. Codex discovers this file automatically at
<repo>/.codex/hooks.json, so it is ZERO-SETUP: clone the repo and the
hook is live for any codex session. No copy-paste, no manual step.
WHAT IT DOES: after every tool call, the PostToolUse hook runs
scripts/code_review_gate.py --mode codex-hook. The script reads this
hook's JSON payload on stdin, and:
* no-ops silently unless the tool call was a `git push`;
* on a `git push`, runs the mechanical review gates (lint +
architecture + V1.34 parity) and writes a JSON response — on
success an `additionalContext` instruction that re-prompts the
codex model to perform the code review as ONE TARGETED AGENT PER
DIMENSION in parallel (one agent per dimension in the skill's
'Execution model' table — architecture, house style, parity/tests,
side effects, observability, abstraction reuse, docs freshness, and
string-literal/env/maintainability/execution-shape/learning),
then synthesize into one verdict; on failure a `decision: block`
carrying the failure reason.
WHY a `command` hook and not an `agent` hook: codex currently runs only
`type: command` handlers — `prompt` and `agent` handlers are parsed but
SKIPPED. So the hook cannot dispatch the code-reviewer agent directly.
Instead the command hook injects the per-dimension fan-out review
instruction back into the model's context via `additionalContext`.
Claude Code, by contrast, uses
a native `agent` hook in .claude/settings.json — same review, different
wiring. See docs/CODE_REVIEW_HOOK_SETUP.md for the full picture.
The matcher fires on the Bash/shell tool name (codex matchers match the
tool name, not the command string); the script itself filters for
`git push`. The review is ALSO enforced server-side by the CI
`architecture` job, so even a disabled hook never lets a violation
merge.
